verdict: Round 8's changes mostly hold: of 28 L10 findings checked, 27 are resolved as stated. The stranger's path now exists as J1 step 0 with the examples/ starter, and the limits are stated (acceptance only with the maintainer's config repo, catalog reach, GitHub-shaped URLs, VS Code only, secret execution environment, release proof). The delta adds no Blocking or Required defect. Four Advisory items remain.

findings.defect: Round 8 applied L10-8 'as proposed', which included dropping cmux from the examples. J3 is clean and 03 3.4 now uses my-config and shop, but probe A13 still says 'OSC 9 reaching the host terminal/cmux'.
findings.scenario: An adopter whose terminal is not cmux reads A13 and cannot tell whether the probe tests a terminal they have or the maintainer's habit.
findings.change: In A13 write 'the host terminal (cmux is the one the maintainer runs)' or drop the name.

findings.defect: The README prerequisite and 3.5 say the catalog 'covers the reference config repo's stack'. That repository is private, so the sentence gives a stranger no way to tell whether their tools are covered.
findings.scenario: An adopter with a Rust stack reads the README, cannot see the reference stack, and learns the answer only from a failed first sync (07 7.5 step 2).
findings.change: Say 'covers the tools listed in catalog/egress.yaml' in the README outline and in 3.5, and keep the reference-repo origin as a note.

findings.defect: The new rule says user-authored formats change only by a new schema version announced in the release notes, and that the bumping release reads the previous version. It does not say how many versions a release reads for project.v1 and host-settings.v1, or who migrates a config repo.
findings.scenario: An adopter skips two releases; the release they install no longer reads the version in their config repo, and no page said the window or that agents edit the specs.
findings.change: One sentence in 03's opening: the window for user-authored formats (for example, current and previous), and that the release notes carry the edit to make.

findings.defect: Product-facing text carries review-record ids and a maintainer-instance default. The 5.4 row cites 'R8-01-16', and Q13's default says the reference instance binds the operator's own token (ADR 0008), the pointer L10-4 asked to remove from product text.
findings.scenario: An adopter reading 5.4 or Q13 meets an id they cannot resolve and an ADR about someone else's token.
findings.change: Cite the decision date only in the 5.4 row, and end Q13's default after 'written per project'.

pages_read: docs/reviews/round-8.md (L10 rows, decisions SC2, SC16, AR6, AR23, DR2)
out_of_scope: Four parked plan findings (L10-29 to L10-32), carried to stage B. Deferred decisions, non-goals and accepted risks as written. Not run: whether the examples/ starter is complete and whether op works under env -i, which need code and a host.
confidence: Medium-high. Every round-8 resolution was checked against the baseline text. The delta was skimmed outside the pages the lens names.
